About the project

HAB-PLAN — Smart decisions for the future of space exploration

An autonomous rover that analyses how habitable an environment is by collecting and interpreting the data essential for assessing future human colonisation of planets or natural satellites.

Tudor Mătăsaru Teodor Preda Coord. Prof. Ioana Stoica

The mission

HAB-PLAN reads seven environmental parameters and combines them into a single Habitability Index between 0 and 1. The closer to 1, the closer the environment is to one that could sustain human life.

The rover hardware combines a Raspberry Pi (Sense HAT), Arduino UNO and Arduino Mega 2560, plus gas, climate, ultrasonic, magnetometer and muon sensors. It is controlled remotely over the local network from this web interface.

How the index is built

Each parameter is mapped through an asymmetric Gaussian centred on its biologically optimal value, using different deviations for under-shoot and over-shoot. That yields a score between 0 and 1 per parameter.

The seven scores are combined into a weighted geometric mean — the weights reflect how critical each parameter is to human survival. The formula:

HI = ∏ Iₖ^(wₖ) with ∑ wₖ = 1.

Using this dashboard

  • Home — drive the rover; hold a direction button to keep moving.
  • Data → Export CSV — save the current recording to disk.
  • Data → Import CSV — replay a recording in read-only playback mode.

Configure the rover endpoint with REACT_APP_ROBOT_URL at build time, e.g. http://AstroVianu.local:8080.
